editorial:
Imagine waking up every day not knowing if what you see is real or just a trick of your mind. You follow a teenage girl who deals with schizophrenia and feels like the world is closing in on her. She becomes convinced that her neighbor is hiding a kidnapped child, but since she struggles with her mental health, nobody believes her. Her parents are trying their best to keep things stable, but they have their own dark family secrets that they are hiding from her. It creates a really tense mood where you are constantly guessing who is lying and who is telling the truth.

The acting is the best part here because you really feel the girl's confusion and fear. While the story starts a bit slow, the twists at the end make the ride worth it. Some parts might feel a bit repetitive, but if you like mysteries that mess with your head, you will love this.
endingExplained: You find out that the girl's suspicions about the neighbor were actually right, but there is a bigger twist involving her family. It turns out her parents were covering up a tragedy from their own past. The boy, Caleb, was a manifestation of her mind helping her uncover the truth. In the end, the truth about the missing child comes out, and she finally finds some peace by facing the lies her parents told her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological mysteries and twist endings.
